parts.title: Part II – Completion and Work Out Questions
parts.instructions: Part II contains five completion questions (A1–A5, 2 points each) and four work out questions (B1–B4, show all necessary steps). In this bank A1–A5 are numbered 1–5 and B1–B4 are numbered 6–9.

All answers were solved independently, every calculation (including the similar questions) was checked with sympy (tools/src_matric/mathematics_2019/verify.py), and the method follows the Eritrean MoE Mathematics textbooks Grades 9–12. See confidence and review_flag on each question.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a subset of the set A = {∅, x, y}?
explanation_steps: A subset must itself be a set whose elements all belong to A.
∅ is a subset of every set; {x} ⊆ A because x ∈ A; {∅} ⊆ A because ∅ is an element of A.
y is an ELEMENT of A (y ∈ A), not a set of elements of A, so y is not a subset. Answer: C.
tips: Distinguish ∈ (element of) from ⊆ (subset of).
Here ∅ is both an element of A and a subset of A.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is not a subset of B = {1, {2}, 3}?
explanation_steps: The elements of B are 1, {2} and 3; the number 2 itself is not an element.
So {2} ⊄ B, while {{2}} ⊆ B. Answer: C.
Only statement A is true. Answer: A.
tips: Test each option separately – differences first, then intersections.

similar_questions.stem: If P = {a, b, c}, Q = {b, c, d} and R = {c, d, e}, which is true?
explanation_steps: Q − P = {d}, ∩ R = {d}; R − P = {d, e}, ∩ Q = {d}; P − R = {a, b}, ∩ Q = {b}. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following relations is not a function?

options.A: R = {(x, y): x is the price of an article y}
options.B: R = {(x, y): x is the perimeter of triangle y}
options.C: R = {(x, y): y is the multiple of x}
options.D: R = {(x, y): x is the plate number of car y}

explanation_steps: A relation is a function if each first element x is paired with exactly one second element y.
In C, a number x has many multiples (x, 2x, 3x, …), so the same x is paired with many y – not a function; the reverse relation (each y with its divisors) is not a function either.
A plate number belongs to exactly one car (D is a function). Answer: C.
tips: Test with a counter-example: x = 2 is paired with y = 4 and y = 6.

similar_questions.stem: Which relation is a function?

options.A: {(x, y): y is a factor of x}
options.E: {(x, y): x is a brother of y}

explanation_steps: y = x² gives one y for every x.
The others pair one x with several y. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Strictly (x → y), A and B are also not functions: many articles can have the same price and many triangles the same perimeter. Under the reverse reading (each article/triangle/car has one price/perimeter/plate) only C fails, so C is the only option that is not a function under either reading. Keyed C – teacher to confirm.

questions.stem: The solution set of (3x − 1)/2 ≤ (4 − x)/3 is
explanation_steps: The correct solution set {x : x ≤ 1} is not among the options.
If the right-hand side were (4 + x)/3: 9x − 3 ≤ 8 + 2x → 7x ≤ 11 → x ≤ 11/7, which is option B – the evident intended answer.
tips: Multiply both sides by the LCD (6) – a positive number, so the inequality sign stays.
questions.review_flag: As printed the solution is x ≤ 1, which is not an option. Option B (x ≤ 11/7) results if the numerator is 4 + x (probable misprint). Keyed B – teacher decision / consider voiding.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = x − 1 be two real functions. Then which of the following is false?
questions.stem_tex: Let $f(x)=x^{2}+1$ and $g(x)=x-1$. Which is false? (A) $(f+g)(x)=x^{2}+x$ (B) $(fg)(x)=x^{3}-x^{2}+x-1$ (C) $(f-g)(x)=x^{2}-x+2$ (D) $\left(\dfrac{f}{g}\right)(x)=x+1,\ x\ne1$
explanation_steps: f/g = (x² + 1)/(x − 1); x² + 1 does not factor, so it is NOT x + 1 (that would need x² − 1). Answer: D.
tips: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1) but x² + 1 has no real factors.

questions.stem: The solution set of x^(1/4) − 3x^(1/2) + 2 = 0 is
explanation_steps: Let t = x^(1/4) ≥ 0, so x^(1/2) = t². The equation becomes t − 3t² + 2 = 0 → 3t² − t − 2 = 0 → (3t + 2)(t − 1) = 0.
tips: Substitute t for the smallest fractional power to get a quadratic.
Reject negative values of an even root.
questions.review_flag: If the exponents were intended the other way round (x^(1/2) − 3x^(1/4) + 2 = 0) the solutions would be 1 and 16 (answer E). Keyed as printed: A.

explanation_steps: Let the number be 10a + b. Then 10a + b = 3(a + b) → 7a = 2b.
From 7a = 2b and b = a + 5: 7a = 2a + 10 → a = 2, b = 7. The number is 27 (check 27 = 3 × 9, 27 + 45 = 72 ✓). Answer: C.
tips: Reversing the digits changes the number by 9 × (difference of digits).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a polynomial function?
questions.stem_tex: Which is not a polynomial function? (A) $2x^4-x^2+5x+6$ (B) $\sqrt2\,x^3-\pi x^2-4x+2$ (C) $\sqrt{(x^2+3)^2}$ (D) $\dfrac{(x-3)^3}{x-3}$
explanation_steps: A and B are polynomials (coefficients such as √2 and π may be any real numbers).
C: √((x² + 3)²) = |x² + 3| = x² + 3 for all x – a polynomial.
D equals (x − 3)² only for x ≠ 3; it is undefined at x = 3, so its domain is not ℝ and it is not a polynomial function. Answer: D.
tips: A polynomial function is defined for every real number and has only non-negative whole-number powers of x.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a polynomial function?
explanation_steps: Only D has whole-number powers and real coefficients for every x.

questions.stem: The simplified form of 1/log(base xy)(xyz) + 1/log(base yz)(xyz) + 1/log(base xz)(xyz) is
explanation_steps: 1/logₐb = log(base b)a, so the sum is log(base xyz)(xy) + log(base xyz)(yz) + log(base xyz)(xz).
= log(base xyz)(xy · yz · xz) = log(base xyz)(x²y²z²) = log(base xyz)((xyz)²) = 2. Answer: D.
tips: Reciprocal rule: logₐb · log(base b)a = 1.

explanation_steps: = log(base abc) a + log(base abc) b + log(base abc) c = log(base abc)(abc) = 1.

explanation_steps: Critical points x = 0 and x = 1/3. Sign test: x < 0 → negative ✓; 0 < x < 1/3 → positive ✗; x > 1/3 → negative ✓.

questions.stem: The inverse of the function f = {(x, y): y = x² − 9, x < 0} is
explanation_steps: Swap x and y: x = y² − 9 with y < 0 → y² = x + 9 → y = −√(x + 9) (negative root because y < 0).
Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f = {x : x > −9}. Option B has the correct rule. Answer: B.
tips: The restriction x < 0 on f becomes y < 0 on f⁻¹, which fixes the sign of the root.

similar_questions.stem: Find the inverse of f(x) = x² + 1, x ≥ 0.
explanation_steps: Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f = [1, ∞). Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: Strictly the domain of f⁻¹ is x > −9 (since x < 0 excludes y = −9 from the range of f); option B writes x ≥ −9. B is still clearly the intended answer.

Areas of equilateral triangles are proportional to the squares of their sides: (s/a)² = 4/3. Answer: B.
tips: For similar figures, area ratio = (side ratio)².

questions.stem: In the figure, BD ⊥ AC and CE ⊥ AB (D on AC, E on AB, BD and CE meet at F). Then which of the following is not true?

explanation_steps: A: △AEC and △ADB are right-angled (at E and D) and share ∠A → similar (AA) ✓.
B: △BEF and △CDF are right-angled (at E and D) with vertical angles at F → similar ✓.  C: angle sum of a triangle ✓.
D: from △AEC ~ △ADB, AE/AD = EC/DB = AC/AB, so AC/AB = CE/BD ✓.
All four statements are true. Answer: E.
tips: Write the correspondence in order (A↔A, E↔D, C↔B) before forming ratios.

questions.stem: The sides of a triangle are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. The area of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of the sides of the triangle, in square cm, is
explanation_steps: 3² + 4² = 5², so the triangle is right-angled with area ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 cm².
The mid-point triangle has sides half as long (mid-point theorem), so its area is (½)² = ¼ of the original: 6/4 = 1.5 cm². Answer: B.
tips: The four small triangles formed by the mid-segments are congruent.

questions.stem: The ratio of the radius of the circumscribed circle of a regular hexagon to the radius of the circumscribed circle of an equilateral triangle, having equal perimeters, is
explanation_steps: Let the common perimeter be 6a. Hexagon side = a; its circumradius equals its side: R₁ = a.
R₁/R₂ = a ÷ (2a/√3) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866, which is not among A–D. Answer: E.
tips: Circumradius of a regular hexagon = side; of an equilateral triangle = side/√3.

questions.stem: Let △STU be similar to △QPR. If ST = 3 cm, TU = 7 cm and QP = 12 cm, then PR = ____ cm.
explanation_steps: Correspondence S↔Q, T↔P, U↔R, so ST ↔ QP and TU ↔ PR.
Scale factor QP/ST = 12/3 = 4 → PR = 4 × 7 = 28 cm. Answer: B.
tips: The order of letters in a similarity statement tells you which sides correspond.

questions.stem: If quadrilateral ABCD is a trapezoid (AB ∥ CD, with diagonals AD and BC meeting at O as in the figure), then which of the following statements is false?
questions.image_alt: Trapezoid with the short side AB at the top (A left, B right) and the long side CD at the bottom (C left, D right); segments AC and BD are the legs, and AD and BC are the diagonals crossing at O.

options.B: If the non-parallel sides are congruent, then ∠C ≅ ∠D.
options.C: If the non-parallel sides are congruent, then the diagonals are congruent.

explanation_steps: AB ∥ CD gives △AOB ~ △DOC, so AO/DO = BO/CO = AB/DC – A is true.
In an isosceles trapezoid (AC = BD) the base angles are equal and the diagonals are equal – B and C are true.
△ACD ≅ △BDC needs AC = BD and AD = BC, which hold only for an isosceles trapezoid; for a general trapezoid D is false. Answer: D.
tips: A statement that is true only in a special case is 'false' as a general statement.

questions.stem:
B1. The following table consists of scores obtained in a class quiz out of 10.
Score: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9
Frequency (# students): 1 2 1 1 2 2 5 3 3
1.1 Find a) the mode, b) the median and c) the mean. (2 points)
1.2 Find the standard deviation. (2 points)
1.3 If a student is selected at random from the class, what is the probability that the chosen student gets a pass mark (5 or greater than 5)? (1 point)

stem_tables.title: Scores in a class quiz (out of 10)

explanation_steps: Mode: the score with the highest frequency (5 students) is 7.
Median: average of the 10th and 11th scores. Cumulative frequencies 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 14, … – both the 10th and 11th scores are 7, so the median is 7.
Standard deviation (textbook population formula σ = √(Σf(x − x̄)²/N)): Σf(x − x̄)² = 25 + 32 + 9 + 4 + 2 + 0 + 5 + 12 + 27 = 116; σ² = 116/20 = 5.8; σ = √5.8 ≈ 2.41.
marking_points: 1.2: Σf(x − x̄)² = 116 (1); σ = √5.8 ≈ 2.41 (1). Accept √(116/19) ≈ 2.47 if the sample formula is used consistently.
tips: Build a table with columns x, f, fx, (x − x̄)² f to avoid arithmetic slips.
With an even N the median is the mean of the two middle values.

similar_questions.stem: For the data 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 8, find the mean and the (population) standard deviation.

questions.review_flag: The textbook uses the population standard deviation (divide by N), giving ≈ 2.41; a sample SD (divide by N − 1) gives ≈ 2.47 – teachers may accept either.

questions.stem:
B2. Given a regular square pyramid with a height of 6 cm and a slant height of 10 cm, find the
2.1 lateral area of the square pyramid. (1 point)
2.2 total surface area of the square pyramid. (1 point)
2.3 volume of the pyramid. (1 point)
questions.answer: Half the base edge = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm, so the base edge is 16 cm. 2.1 Lateral area = 320 cm². 2.2 Total surface area = 576 cm². 2.3 Volume = 512 cm³.
explanation_steps: The height (6), the slant height (10) and half the base edge form a right triangle: half-edge = √(100 − 36) = 8 cm → base edge a = 16 cm.
Lateral area = 4 × ½ × a × slant height = 4 × ½ × 16 × 10 = 320 cm².
Total surface area = lateral area + base = 320 + 16² = 320 + 256 = 576 cm².
Volume = ⅓ × base area × height = ⅓ × 256 × 6 = 512 cm³.
marking_points: Finding the base edge 16 cm is needed for all parts.
tips: The slant height is measured on a face, from the apex to the midpoint of a base edge.

B3. Given the rational function f(x) = (3x − 6)/(x − 4), then
3.1 find its domain and range. (1 point)
3.2 find its asymptotes. (1 point)
3.3 sketch its graph. (2 points)
questions.stem_tex: B3. Given the rational function $f(x)=\dfrac{3x-6}{x-4}$: 3.1 find its domain and range; 3.2 find its asymptotes; 3.3 sketch its graph.
questions.answer: 3.1 Domain {x ∈ ℝ : x ≠ 4}; range {y ∈ ℝ : y ≠ 3}. 3.2 Vertical asymptote x = 4; horizontal asymptote y = 3. 3.3 Hyperbola with intercepts (2, 0) and (0, 3/2), lying in the upper-right and lower-left regions formed by the asymptotes.

subparts.question: Sketch
subparts.answer: Two branches about the asymptotes x = 4, y = 3 through (2, 0) and (0, 1.5)
steps: Plot intercepts and a few points on each side of x = 4.

explanation_steps: Write f(x) = 3 + 6/(x − 4). Since 6/(x − 4) is never 0, f(x) ≠ 3; every other value is taken → range ℝ \ {3}.
Vertical asymptote x = 4 (denominator zero, numerator 6 ≠ 0). Horizontal asymptote y = 3 (ratio of leading coefficients 3/1).
Extra points: f(5) = 9, f(6) = 6, f(3) = −3, f(−2) = 2. For x > 4 the curve is above y = 3; for x < 4 it is below y = 3.
Sketch: dashed lines x = 4 and y = 3; the right branch comes down from +∞ near x = 4 towards y = 3; the left branch passes through (0, 1.5) and (2, 0) and falls to −∞ as x → 4⁻.
marking_points: 3.3: asymptotes drawn (0.5), intercepts (0.5), both branches correct in shape and position (1).
tips: Rewrite as a constant plus a proper fraction to read off the horizontal asymptote and the range.

questions.stem: B4. In the figure, MP ≅ NQ and ∠KPQ ≅ ∠KQP (M, P, Q, N collinear in that order; K is the apex). Show that △MNK is an isosceles triangle. (3 points)
questions.image_alt: Triangle MNK with base MN; points P and Q on MN (order M, P, Q, N); segments KP and KQ drawn from the apex K.
questions.answer: Since ∠KPQ ≅ ∠KQP, △KPQ is isosceles, so KP ≅ KQ. The angles ∠KPM and ∠KQN are supplements of the equal angles ∠KPQ and ∠KQP, so ∠KPM ≅ ∠KQN. With MP ≅ NQ, △KPM ≅ △KQN (SAS). Hence KM ≅ KN (CPCTC), so △MNK is isosceles.
explanation_steps: 5. Therefore KM ≅ KN (corresponding parts of congruent triangles), so △MNK is isosceles with KM = KN.
marking_points: KP ≅ KQ from the equal base angles (1).
tips: Supplements of equal angles are equal.
Alternative: MQ = MP + PQ = NQ + QP = NP, and △KMQ ≅ △KNP by SAS.

explanation_steps: Supplements are equal; SAS congruence; CPCTC.
